A random system produces outcomes that are not determined in advance, although they may fall within a defined probability range. Its unpredictability comes from chance rather than from sensitivity in a deterministic rule set.

This distinguishes it from a [[Chaotic System]]. Games use [[Randomization]] to stand in for systems that are too detailed to model and to introduce uncertainty into [[Meaningful Decision|meaningful decisions]].

A random variable assigns a numerical value to the outcome of a random process. Its realized value changes across repeated samples or experiments even when the underlying population and procedure remain fixed.

The source treats sample means, mean differences, test statistics, and p-values as random variables. Recognizing this variability is essential because an observed estimate is one realization from a [[Sampling Distribution]], not the population quantity itself.

A randomized algorithm deliberately uses chance when selecting part of its execution path. Its result or runtime can vary between runs even when the input is unchanged.

Randomness can avoid consistently unfavorable deterministic choices. [[Quicksort]] selects pivots randomly so that its expected complexity is loglinear, even though a theoretically possible sequence of extreme pivots would be much slower. Correct sorting is guaranteed; chance affects performance rather than correctness.

A rare event Poisson approximation replaces a [[Binomial Distribution]] with a [[Poisson Distribution]] when the number of trials is large, the success probability is small, and their product remains a moderate expected count.

The approximation captures the asymmetric distribution near zero that a normal approximation cannot represent well. Its Poisson rate equals the binomial expected count, preserving the relevant event scale while simplifying calculation.

A raster attribute table associates integer raster cell codes with category labels and possibly additional class attributes. It lets a [[Categorical Raster Map]] display meaningful names instead of raw numbers and supports selecting a qualitative palette by class. The table does not change cell geometry; it supplies semantics for stored values. Codes, labels, and colors should remain synchronized when classes are merged or reordered.

A raster map animation plots each layer of a time-indexed raster with the same graphical settings and concatenates the resulting image files into a movie. It can reveal movement of a continuous field, such as forecast cloud cover, when adjacent layers change smoothly. Administrative boundaries supply fixed spatial context. Inconsistent scales or extents would turn frame-to-frame changes in rendering into apparent changes in the data.

A raster marginal summary aggregates cell values along rows or columns and plots the result beside a [[Quantitative Raster Map]]. It reveals broad variation by latitude or longitude that may be difficult to isolate in the full two-dimensional pattern. The summary function may be a mean, median, or another statistic, and missing cells must be handled consistently. Margins reduce spatial detail, so they complement rather than replace the map.

A rate written as a quotient must convert numerator and denominator in positions that leave the target units. For example, a volume-per-day value needs a volume ratio and a day-to-second ratio oriented inversely because time sits below the fraction line. Pryor's flow, velocity, power, and fuel-efficiency examples all use this same unit algebra even though their physical meanings differ. Checking cancellation prevents a factor of 60 or 3,600 from being accidentally applied in the wrong direction. See [[Conversion-Factor Chains]].

A rater policy is the functional relationship a judge appears to use when converting a profile of predictor values into an overall decision. Judgmental analysis represents that relationship through a multiple-regression equation.

Comparing equations reveals whether judges share a policy even when their individual ratings differ. The result preserves both the direction and relative importance of the predictors.

A rational exponent connects powers and roots: $a^{m/n}=(\sqrt[n]{a})^m$ when the real root is defined. The denominator selects the root and the numerator selects the power. These definitions extend the [[Exponent Laws]], but even roots impose nonnegative-radicand restrictions when calculations remain in the real numbers.

A rational expression is a quotient of algebraic expressions, commonly polynomials:

$$\frac{P(x)}{Q(x)},\qquad Q(x)\neq0.$$

It generalizes a numerical [[Fraction]] while retaining the restriction that its denominator cannot be zero. Operations follow fraction rules, but polynomial factorization is often required before cancellation or construction of a common denominator. Equivalent-looking simplified forms must preserve the original excluded values because cancelling a factor does not make the original denominator defined there.

A rational expression is undefined at any value that makes its denominator zero. Before simplifying

$$\frac{x^2-1}{x-1},$$

the value (x=1) must be excluded. Factoring and cancelling gives (x+1), but the original expression still has no value at (x=1).

Restrictions should therefore be identified before cancellation, multiplication, or cross multiplication. A transformation can preserve equality only on the domain where every expression and division used in the step is defined.

A rational function is a quotient $f(x)=p(x)/q(x)$ of polynomials with $q(x)\ne0$. Zeros of the denominator are excluded from its domain and may produce holes or [[Vertical Asymptote]]s. Comparing polynomial degrees helps determine end behavior and possible [[Horizontal Asymptote]]s.

A rational inequality compares a [[Rational Expression]] with zero or another expression. Zeros of the numerator and denominator divide the number line into sign intervals, but denominator zeros are always excluded. A sign chart avoids unsafe cross-multiplication by a quantity whose sign may be unknown.

A rational number is a number expressible as a quotient of two integers,

$$\frac{a}{b},\qquad b\neq0.$$

Rational numbers include integers and positive or negative [[Fraction]]s. They are closed under addition, subtraction, and multiplication, and under division by a nonzero rational number. In positional decimal notation, every rational number has an expansion that either terminates or eventually repeats. Conversely, a terminating or [[Repeating Decimal]] represents a rational number.

A raw attribute is recorded directly from a source; a derived attribute is calculated from other fields. Derivation can encode a meaningful interaction that no single raw field expresses. The book uses body mass index, calculated from weight and height, to illustrate how a combined measure may relate more strongly to a study target than either input alone.

Derived features still need domain scrutiny. A useful calculation for one setting may be unhelpful elsewhere, and an inappropriate transformation can hide differences. Feature design is part of representing the problem, not just a technical optimization after data collection.

A raw Ethernet storage protocol places storage-specific messages directly in Ethernet frames instead of passing every request through a full general-purpose network stack. The shorter path can reduce processing, copies, and latency for small I/O.

The protocol must supply any required reliability, addressing, flow control, and request matching that higher layers would otherwise provide.

A Razor layout defines the shared outer structure of multiple pages or views, such as navigation, metadata, scripts, and a common visual shell. Each content page supplies its body and may define named sections consumed by the layout.

Layouts reduce duplicated markup and create a single place for application-wide presentation changes. Shared view imports and startup files can further establish common namespaces, tag helpers, and default layout choices.

A Razor Page pairs a `.cshtml` template with an optional page-model class that contains request handlers, bound properties, and presentation logic. Handler methods correspond to HTTP operations and can prepare the data rendered by the page.

The page-centered structure keeps the code for one screen close together while still separating C# behavior from markup. Services supplied through dependency injection let the page model coordinate persistence or application logic without constructing its dependencies directly.

A React component prop is an input passed from a consuming component to a child component. Props make a component configurable in the same way that function parameters make a function reusable.

TypeScript interfaces can specify prop names and types, including callback functions. A component reads its props when rendering but does not treat them as its own mutable state.

A React element is an object describing what should appear at one position in the interface tree. JSX expressions produce these element descriptions for intrinsic browser elements or for other React components.

Elements are descriptions rather than mutable document nodes. React compares the newly produced tree with the prior rendering and applies the required browser updates.

A React form coordinates controlled field values, validation state, submission progress, and success or failure behavior. The browser form event is handled by component logic so the application can validate and send data without an automatic page navigation.

Reusable form and field components reduce repeated state and event code. Server-side validation remains necessary even when the React form provides complete client feedback.

A React Router Link renders navigable content that changes the client-side location without forcing a full document request. It preserves browser navigation behavior while letting the router select the destination component.

Links are appropriate when navigation is part of rendered content. An event handler that decides a destination after work completes can use [[Programmatic Navigation]] instead.

A reactive assistant acts in response to an explicit user request or event. The user initiates the exchange, so the immediate purpose of the interaction is comparatively clear.

Reactive behavior limits interruption and privacy risks, but it cannot surface useful information before the user thinks to ask. A [[Proactive Assistant]] takes the stronger step of initiating an interaction.

A reactive stream is a time-ordered sequence of notifications. It may emit values, report an error, and signal completion, so a consumer must consider more than the next ordinary value. User events, inventory updates, and calculated totals can each be treated as streams. Operators can derive new streams without requiring producers to know every downstream consumer.

A reactive system is an architectural arrangement designed to remain responsive under changing load and partial failure. The book describes responsiveness, scalability, resilience, and message-based communication as its related properties. This is broader than using an observable sequence inside one process: component boundaries, resource allocation, and failure isolation determine whether the whole service can keep responding.

A read model is a data representation shaped for a specific information need. An [[Application Query]] retrieves it without invoking state-changing domain behavior, and the API can often return the stored shape directly without mapping it through an [[Aggregate]]. Read models can combine fields from several aggregates and use indexes or denormalization suited to their consumers. In event-sourced systems, a [[Projection]] builds and updates them from domain events.

A real number is any [[Rational Number]] or [[Irrational Number]]. The real numbers fill the [[Number Line]]: each point corresponds to a real value, and order corresponds to position from left to right.

Elementary algebra generally treats variables as real unless another domain is specified. The real-number system supports addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by nonzero values, along with order comparisons. Restrictions still matter; for example, a denominator cannot equal zero, and an even root is not a real number when its radicand is negative.

A real square matrix $Q$ is orthogonal when $Q^TQ=QQ^T=I$, so $Q^{-1}=Q^T$. Its columns and rows form orthonormal sets.

Orthogonal transformations preserve vector lengths and angles. This makes them numerically valuable in [[QR Decomposition]], [[Orthogonal Diagonalization]], [[Givens Rotation]], and [[Householder Transformation]].

A real square matrix is skew-symmetric when $A^T=-A$. Every diagonal entry must therefore be zero.

The condition is checked by comparing corresponding entries across the main diagonal: $a_{ij}=-a_{ji}$. This distinguishes skew symmetry from the mirrored equality of a [[Symmetric Matrix]].

A real square matrix is symmetric when $A^T=A$. Its entries mirror across the main diagonal.

Symmetric matrices have real eigenvalues and admit an orthonormal set of eigenvectors, enabling [[Orthogonal Diagonalization]]. They also arise as [[Hessian Matrix|Hessian matrices]], normal-equation matrices, and positive-definite coefficient matrices.

A real symmetric matrix $A$ is positive definite when $x^TAx>0$ for every nonzero vector $x$. Its eigenvalues are positive.

Positive definiteness guarantees important numerical behavior: [[Cholesky Decomposition]] exists, the [[Conjugate Gradient Method]] has a suitable energy minimization interpretation, and a positive-definite [[Hessian Matrix]] identifies a strict local minimum.

A real-time API allows the server to deliver an event to a client without waiting for that client to poll another request. It is useful when the value of a screen changes because of activity elsewhere in the system.

The contract defines connection setup as well as message names and payloads. Clients must map each message into their own state and remain prepared for connection failure or interruption.

A receiver operating characteristic curve plots true-positive rate against false-positive rate as the decision threshold of a probabilistic binary classifier varies. Each point represents a different discrete operating rule.

Curves toward the upper-left indicate stronger separation, and the area under the curve summarizes ranking performance across thresholds. Operational selection still requires a specific balance between missed positives and false alarms.

The book uses ROC curves to compare predictive models across possible probability cutoffs rather than fixing one threshold prematurely. It pairs the curve with area under the curve and risk-oriented displays that connect ranking quality to use.

A recently popular method of an fMRI experiment, known as resting state fMRI (rs-fMRI),
involves measuring blood oxygenation while not performing any explicit task. This method was
first described by Biswal et al. [13], in which he explored the relationships between brain regions
rather than the application of explicit tasks to find regions associated with those tasks.
The signal strength in fMRI is low and requires elaborate processing to be able to extract use-
ful information from the recorded data from an MR machine. Similar to any measurement system,
there is system noise in the recorded signal. This includes thermal noise, RF-induced noise, noise
introduced while signal amplification and other system-related processes that cause system insta-
bility. In addition to the system noise, there is also a physiological noise induced by changes in the
physiology of the human (or animal) subject. This includes noise introduced due to motion (of the
human) during scanning, signal fluctuations induced by cardiac pulsation, signal fluctuations due
to magnetic field change induced by the amount of air in the lungs (respiration), and fluctuations
in hematocrit content in the blood that influences the magnetic properties of the tissue and several
others. While it is difficult to entirely eliminate noise, the attempt is to maximize sensitivity and
specificity by reducing the effects of noise.

A receptive field is the limited region of an input image inspected by one neuron in a [[Convolutional Neural Network]]. Early convolutional neurons take values from small neighboring pixel patches rather than the whole image. Neurons that share a detector can be placed at different positions, so their receptive fields collectively search for the same local feature across the image.

Neighboring fields may overlap. Their separation is controlled by [[Convolutional Stride]]. Later layers can combine responses from multiple local fields into features with broader spatial scope. The field is therefore an architectural choice about which input relationships a neuron can use directly.

A recommender system predicts or ranks items that may be useful to a user from observed preferences, item information, or interactions. Its output reduces a large choice space to a personalized set of candidates.

Different systems rely on [[Collaborative Filtering]], [[Content-Based Recommendation]], or a hybrid. The appropriate design depends on available feedback, scale, changing context, and how recommendation quality will be evaluated.

A record exclusion audit preserves or counts observations removed by each filtering rule. Instead of viewing exclusion as a silent side effect, the analyst records why rows left the analysis and how many were affected.

The audit can reveal selection bias, especially when a required measure is missing for most people with the outcome. It also supports rollback and verification by showing that retained and excluded partitions reconcile with the input dataset.

Removing observations with a missing target is a consequential modeling decision in the book's preparation workflow. Recording the affected rows and counts distinguishes a justified analytic population from an accidental loss of data.

A recovery point objective is the maximum targeted age of data that may be lost when a system is restored after disruption. It describes how far back in time the recovered state may be compared with the moment of failure.

The objective determines how frequently data must be replicated or backed up. It is distinct from [[Recovery Time Objective]], which measures the acceptable duration of the outage rather than the acceptable amount of lost history.

A recovery time objective is the maximum targeted interval between a service disruption and restoration of usable service. It answers how long the organization can tolerate the affected system remaining unavailable.

The objective should appear in continuity planning and service commitments so recovery capability can be designed and tested. A short recovery time may require ready secondary capacity, automation, and practiced failover rather than relying only on stored backups.

A rectangular matrix has a different number of rows and columns. An $m\times n$ matrix is rectangular when $m\neq n$.

Rectangular coefficient matrices naturally describe [[Overdetermined Linear System|overdetermined]] and [[Underdetermined Linear System|underdetermined]] systems. They do not have ordinary two-sided inverses, but a [[Pseudoinverse]] and [[Least Squares Approximation]] can supply useful generalized solutions.

A recurrence trigger starts a logic app on a repeated schedule. The campaign workflow uses it to check an Excel table at a chosen interval for rows whose intended publication time has arrived.

A shorter interval makes the automation more responsive but causes more workflow executions. Scheduling is therefore both a behavior decision and an operational-cost decision, even when most runs discover no work.

A recurrent network carries a vector of hidden-layer activations from one sequence step into the next. At the current step, the hidden layer receives both the new input and this stored context. Its output is used to produce the current result and to update the state for the following step.

The memory buffer in Kelleher's [[Recurrent Neural Network]] diagram stores activations without transforming them; weighted connections from the buffer to the hidden units perform the next transformation. This feedback lets a later input be processed in the context of earlier inputs, although basic recurrence can struggle to retain long-range information during training.

A recurrent neural network processes a sequence while carrying information from earlier steps into later ones. Its recurrent connections make the current output depend on both the present input and a representation of prior inputs.

This structure fits speech and language, where word or sound interpretation depends on surrounding sequence context. [[Long Short-Term Memory]] units were developed to preserve relevant information across longer spans.

Kelleher depicts the network's [[Recurrent Hidden State|hidden state]] as a memory buffer whose activations are fed into the next step along with its new input. [[Time-Unrolled Recurrent Network|Unrolling]] the loop shows how one set of [[Recurrent Weight Sharing Across Time|shared recurrent weights]] is reused through a sequence. Training with [[Backpropagation Through Time]] then has to propagate error through those steps, which can make long-range dependencies difficult to learn.

A recursive belief update uses the posterior from one step as the prior for the next. A repeated transition-and-observation decomposition prevents the full observation history from having to be reconsidered from scratch.

The same description can answer filtering, prediction, or smoothing questions by changing the time index of the searched state. Its efficiency comes from the Markov assumptions encoded in the decomposition.

A recursive definition specifies initial values and then defines later or larger objects in terms of earlier or smaller ones. The factorial definition fixes 0! = 1 and defines n! = n(n − 1)! for n > 0; the Fibonacci sequence requires two initial values before applying its recurrence.

Because the definition builds an infinite family from finite rules, facts about recursively defined objects are commonly proved with [[Mathematical Induction]] or [[Strong Induction]].

A recursive function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller or simpler input. It requires a base case that returns without another call and a recursive case that makes progress toward that base.

Each call consumes stack space until it returns, so missing or unreachable termination can cause a stack overflow. Recursive definitions can closely match problems such as factorials, but their numeric result can still overflow the chosen return type even when the recursion itself terminates correctly.

A recursive graph feature repeatedly aggregates features from neighboring nodes. Starting with basic properties, each iteration expands the represented context to another graph radius.

This construction can create expressive relational features without naming every motif. Repeated aggregation may blur distinct nodes into similar representations, so depth, aggregation functions, and pruning matter.

A recursive language is a synonym for a [[Turing-Decidable Language]]. Membership is determined by a computation that always halts with either acceptance or rejection.

A language is recursive exactly when both it and its complement are [[Recursively Enumerable Language|recursively enumerable]]. Running their accepting machines in alternating steps guarantees that one halts and reveals the correct decision for each input.

A recursively enumerable language can be listed by a machine that runs indefinitely, eventually outputting every member and no nonmember. The order need not be fixed, and repetitions are allowed.

This class is equivalent to the [[Turing-Acceptable Language|Turing-acceptable languages]], the ranges of Turing-computable enumerating functions, and the languages generated by general grammars. Dovetailing several simulations prevents one nonhalting computation from blocking all later candidates.

A red-cyan anaglyph combines the red channel from one eye view with the green and blue channels from the other. Correspondingly colored filters then present the intended channel combination to each eye. The book demonstrates the assembly by disabling green and blue in the left image layer and red in the right layer. This is a presentation method for a stereo pair, not a way to invent depth from a single identical view. The two viewpoints must first satisfy [[Left- and Right-Eye Image Separation]].

A reduced ring is a ring whose [[Nilradical]] is zero. Equivalently, it has no nonzero [[Nilpotent Element]]s.

Every ring R has a canonical reduced quotient R/N, where N is its nilradical. This quotient preserves the prime-ideal structure while eliminating elements whose powers vanish.

A Redux action creator is a function that constructs an action. Centralizing this construction gives calling code a stable operation and keeps action types and payload shapes from being repeated throughout components.

A synchronous action creator returns an action immediately. With middleware such as Redux Thunk, an action creator can instead coordinate asynchronous work and dispatch later actions as that work progresses.

A Redux action is an object that describes an event that may change application state. Its type identifies what happened, and additional fields carry the data the reducer needs to interpret that event.

Actions describe requested transitions without performing them. Dispatching the action sends it through the store to the reducer, which decides the resulting state.

A Redux provider places the store into React's component context so descendants can access it without passing the store through every intermediate prop. It normally wraps the application near the root of the component tree.

The provider supplies access, while connected components or hooks choose which state and dispatch operations they consume. This keeps the store shared without making every component depend on its entire contents.

A Redux reducer is a pure function that receives the current state and an action and returns the next state. It expresses how each recognized event transforms the store without mutating the existing state object.

Keeping reducers deterministic makes state changes easier to reason about and test. An unrecognized action returns the current state, preserving the store when no transition applies.

A Redux store holds the application's shared state tree and coordinates access to it. It exposes the current state, accepts dispatched actions, and notifies subscribers after the reducer has produced a new state.

The store is the meeting point between action-producing code and state-consuming UI. React components normally receive it through a provider instead of importing a mutable global value.

A reference frame establishes what positions, orientations, and movements are measured relative to.

An egocentric frame is relative to the user's body, such as the eyes, head, torso, hands, or legs, and corresponds to a first-person view. An exocentric frame is relative to an object or the world and corresponds to an outside or third-person view.

In a [[3D User Interface]], changing between egocentric and exocentric views can help different tasks but may also confuse the user. [[Navigation]], [[System Control]], and [[3D Manipulation]] should use a frame that makes their mappings easy to predict.

A reference map helps locate named geographic features such as roads, settlements, boundaries, and landmarks. Its purpose is orientation rather than emphasizing one statistical variable. Web tiles can supply this context beneath a thematic layer, provided the thematic data are transformed to the tile system. Excess detail competes with symbols, so reference content should be selected according to scale and the locations readers need to recognize.

A reflective choice asks the player to consider values, identity, or attitude even though the selected option does not change the plot or game state. Its purpose is to focus attention on the act of choosing and on what that choice means to the player.

Because meaning can arise from interpretation rather than only from mechanical consequence, a reflective choice may affect the experience without altering the outcome. It can ask who the player or character is within the story when no decision can produce a perfect result.

A regenerative fuel-cell arrangement uses available energy to split water into hydrogen and oxygen, then later combines those gases in a [[Fuel Cell]] to make electricity and water again. This makes the reactants a way to store energy across time, rather than a one-way fuel feed. The source illustrates sunlight driving the splitting step, with produced water recirculated for another cycle.

A regional health data platform integrates healthcare information across institutions within a geographic area. It can connect hospital, primary-care, public-health, and administrative records for broader management and analysis.

Integration improves continuity and population-level insight, but it also concentrates sensitive information. Shared definitions, access controls, legal authority, and accountability are necessary for the platform to be trustworthy.

A regression interaction term represents a relationship in which the effect of one explanatory variable depends on the level of another. It is commonly formed as a product while retaining the corresponding lower-order terms.

Once an interaction is included, the lower-order coefficients cannot be interpreted as universal effects. Estimates become stratum-specific combinations of coefficients, so unplanned interaction searches can both inflate false positives and make the model difficult to communicate.

The source constructs interaction columns by multiplying existing design-matrix columns. In R formula syntax, `type:leg` adds only the product terms, while `type*leg` expands to both main effects and their interaction.

A regression reference group is the category against which indicator-variable coefficients are interpreted. Its observations receive zero on every indicator representing the other levels of the same categorical variable.

Choosing a plausible low-risk or otherwise meaningful group can make coefficients easier to explain. Unknown values sometimes remain in the reference group for practical reasons, but doing so changes its meaning and should be disclosed in the model presentation.

The source shows that R's design matrix omits one factor level and places its fitted mean in the intercept. Coefficients for the remaining levels then represent differences from this reference, so changing the reference changes individual coefficient meanings without changing the fitted group means.

A regression residual plot graphs [[Residual|residuals]] against fitted values, predictors, or theoretical quantiles. A well-specified linear model should not leave an obvious trend or systematic change in residual spread.

Curvature can indicate violation of the [[Linearity Assumption]], while a funnel shape suggests nonconstant variance. Quantile–quantile residual plots assess distributional shape, and unusual isolated points may warrant investigation for data errors or influence.

A regular expression is built from ∅, ε, alphabet symbols, union, concatenation, [[Kleene Star]], and grouping. It generates a [[Formal Language]] by interpreting those constructors as the corresponding operations on sets of strings.

A language is regular when some regular expression generates it. Practical search patterns add conveniences such as character classes, optional items, and one-or-more repetition, but features such as backreferences can exceed the power of formal regular expressions.

A regular system of parameters is a [[System of Parameters]] that generates the maximal ideal of a [[Regular Local Ring]]. Its length equals the ring's Krull dimension.

The images of its elements form a basis of m/m² over the residue field, and the elements form a [[Regular Sequence]]. Initial portions reduce the dimension one step at a time while preserving regularity.

A regular time series has observations separated by a constant sampling interval, such as hourly, daily, monthly, or quarterly measurements. Regularity supports predictable alignment and [[Time Series Aggregation]], but it does not guarantee complete data because scheduled observations may still be missing. Calendar-aware indexes such as [[yearmon Time Index]] and [[yearqtr Time Index]] represent common regular periods without pretending that every month or quarter has the same number of days.

A reinforcing loop amplifies the direction of change already occurring in a system. The reinforced quality may be desirable or harmful: growth, learning, disease spread, and accumulating advantage can share the same structure.

In games, reinforcing loops support gain and [[Progression System|progression]], but an unchecked loop can produce a rich-get-richer outcome and collapse the [[Play Space]]. [[Balancing Loop|Balancing loops]] can preserve meaningful competition by limiting runaway divergence.

A relational database management system represents data in relations governed by schemas and supports declarative queries, integrity rules, transactions, and controlled access. The optimizer chooses physical operations for a logical SQL request.

Traditional architectures remain strong for structured data and transactional consistency, but scaling them across massive heterogeneous datasets can require fragmentation, distributed execution, and alternative storage layouts.

A relational database stores data in tables that are mathematical relations: sets of ordered tuples drawn from Cartesian products of data types. Rows are tuples or records, and named columns identify their components.

SQL queries select rows by predicates, project chosen columns, and combine tables through joins that begin from a product and retain matching records. A database management system also supports insertion, deletion, updating, and query optimization.

A relative cluster validity index compares two or more candidate clusterings of the same data. It helps select an algorithm, parameter setting, or number of groups by ranking their fit under one criterion.

The result identifies the best member of the compared set, not necessarily an adequate model in absolute terms. The candidate set and criterion must therefore be reported.

A relative density outlier score compares the density around a point with the average density around its neighbors. A point whose local density is low relative to that context receives a stronger anomaly score.

The comparison provides a ranking rather than only a yes-or-no decision. Selecting k remains difficult, and a direct implementation can require quadratic computation.

A relatively positioned box first receives its ordinary position in normal flow and is then visually shifted by offsets. The space reserved at its original location remains unchanged, so neighboring boxes do not move into the gap or respond to the shifted position.

Relative positioning can also establish a [[CSS Containing Block]] for absolutely positioned descendants. It therefore supports local coordinate systems even when the ancestor itself is not visibly offset.

A relaxation factor $\omega$ controls how strongly an iterative method accepts a newly computed correction. The update combines the previous value with the candidate value.

In [[Successive Over-Relaxation]], $\omega=1$ gives the [[Gauss-Seidel Method]], $0<\omega<1$ gives under-relaxation, and $1<\omega<2$ gives over-relaxation. The best value depends on the problem.

A release pipeline takes versioned build artifacts and installs them into one or more deployment environments. In the book, the flow targets Azure staging resources before promoting a verified release to production.

Separating release from build means the same tested artifact can move between environments. Environment configuration and promotion conditions remain part of the release definition rather than the compiled package.

A reliable track needs a feature that is distinct, contrasted, and visible through the frames being solved. A repeated texture can be confused with another copy of itself; a long straight edge does not uniquely fix movement along that edge; an occluded feature cannot provide continuous evidence. The tracker should preferably be near the depth of the element being attached so parallax does not make the match slide. Choosing the feature well often matters more than enlarging the search region. See [[Tracker Search Window Tuning]].

A rendered object can have correct hue but still differ from the photographed plate in its shadow density, highlight density, or midtone contrast. Per-channel levels adjustments let the compositor compare and move black, white, and gamma values toward nearby plate material. Adjusting only overall brightness can leave colored shadows or highlights visibly wrong. This matching is most useful after shape, perspective, and lighting are plausible; it cannot disguise a camera mismatch. See [[Matching CG Key Fill and Rim Lights]].

A repeating decimal has a finite block of digits that continues indefinitely, such as

$$0.090909\ldots=0.\overline{09}.$$

Every repeating decimal is a [[Rational Number]]. To convert one to a fraction, let a variable equal the decimal, multiply by powers of ten until two forms share the same infinite tail, and subtract. For (x=0.\overline{09}), (100x-x=9), so (99x=9) and (x=1/11). A terminating decimal is also rational because trailing zeros make it a repeating form.

A replaced element is rendered using content outside the document itself, such as an image supplied through a URL or a form control drawn by the user agent. CSS generally treats that external object as a unit with intrinsic dimensions instead of laying out its internal contents.

A nonreplaced element has content represented within the document tree, so CSS constructs and formats boxes for that content directly. The distinction affects sizing, baselines, and inline formatting in the [[CSS Box Model]].

A replaced element supplies externally rendered content and may carry intrinsic width, height, and aspect ratio. CSS uses those intrinsic values when `width` or `height` is automatic, subject to available constraints and any explicit dimensions.

Inline replaced elements enter line layout as a single box with a defined baseline behavior. Their sizing differs from nonreplaced text because the browser is fitting an external object rather than formatting descendant inline content.

Flow Display
The values flow and flow-root deserve a moment of explanation. Declaring an ele‐
ment to be laid out using display: flow means that it should use block-and-inline
layout, the same as normal. That is, unless it’s combined with inline, in which case it
generates an inline box.
310 | Chapter 7: Basic Visual Formatting
In other words, the first two of the following rules will result in a block box, whereas
the third will yield an inline box.
#first {display: flow;}
#second {display: block flow;}
#third {display: inline flow;}
The reason for this pattern is that CSS is moving to a system where there are two
kinds of display: the outer display type and the inner display type. Value keywords like
block and inline represent the outer display type, which provides how the display
box interacts with its surroundings. The inner display, in this case flow, describes
what should happen inside the element.
This approach allows for declarations like display: inline table to indicate an ele‐
ment should generate a table formatting context within, but relate to its surrounding
content as an inline element. (The legacy value inline-table has the same effect.)
display: flow-root, on the other hand, always generates a block box, with a new
block formatting context inside itself. This is the sort of thing that would be applied
to the root element of a document, like html, to say “this is where the formatting root
lies.”

A replacement engine changes both mass and its arm from the aircraft datum. In the Wilga conversion, the longer engine moved its mass forward of the firewall and increased the bending moment even though the engine itself was lighter. Additional support struts, fuel placement, and the final [[Aircraft Center-of-Gravity Calculation]] were needed to reconcile power with structural and balance limits.

A report needs deliberate evidence presentation, which is the concern of [[R Table and Figure Reporting]]. A [[kable Table]] provides a simple rendering of an existing result, while an [[xtable Table]] offers more control over generated markup. [[Booktabs Table Style]] can improve visual hierarchy without heavy grids. [[Table Caption and Label]] and [[Figure Caption and Label]] make tables and graphics referable parts of the argument. [[Figure Chunk Dimensions]] control how a graphic is drawn; [[Figure Output Dimensions]] control its displayed size. [[Figure Placement]] and [[Floating Table]] behavior must balance page layout with proximity to the interpreting prose. [[knitr Global Chunk Options]] establish consistent defaults while allowing justified local exceptions.

[[R Coding Style]] makes all of this easier to read. Stable [[R Script File Naming]], [[R Support Function File Naming]], and [[R Data File Naming]] communicate what files contain. An [[Ordered R Script Prefix]] can reveal an intended pipeline. Consistent [[R Function Naming]], [[R Variable Naming]], and [[R Function Argument Naming]] reduce ambiguity within code. [[R Code Comment Style]] should explain purpose and assumptions rather than paraphrase syntax, while [[R Code Layout]] uses indentation, spaces, braces, and manageable line lengths to expose structure.

Together, environment, functions, literate reports, evidence formatting, and style form one reproducibility system. Clean functions without recorded inputs remain hard to rerun; executable reports with hidden global dependencies remain fragile; correct code with inconsistent names remains difficult to maintain. The practical standard is a project whose data path, computations, outputs, and explanations can be followed as one coherent argument.

A representative player is a hypothetical person who typifies the intended target audience. The designer uses this figure to evaluate whether a proposed feature, challenge, interface, or theme serves the experience being built.

The representative is a decision aid rather than a stereotype or claim about every customer. It should be grounded in audience research and revised when observation contradicts the assumptions behind it.

A reproducible data split can be regenerated from the same source data, random seed, and partition rule. Preserving indices is even stronger because it records the exact membership of each subset.

Reproducibility lets model comparisons use identical cases rather than attributing differences to changing samples.
